title: Signature Upgrade Provenance Record
description: Signature edition: every upgrade decision is recorded with its full reasoning — which advisory triggered it, what tests ran, who approved, what the canary showed. Future teams can audit why a version was chosen, not just that it was. This is a Signature original method.
method: Each upgrade files (trigger, evidence, approver, canary results); the record links to the advisory and test reports; queries answer 'why are we on this version?'
usage: File records automatically from the sentinel flow; review them during incidents involving dependencies.

title: Signature Compatibility test harness
description: Signature edition: Before any upgrade merges, the sentinel runs the project's full test suite plus API-compatibility checks against the new version in an isolated environment. The upgrade PR carries its own evidence: tests green, no removed APIs used, benchmarks within band — merge with confidence or block with specifics.
method: Build a matrix job per upgrade PR (old vs new); run unit, integration, and API-diff checks; attach results to the PR; block on failures.
usage: Keep the harness fast (upgrade PRs are frequent); make failures point at the breaking change specifically.

demo.code:
print('upgrade PR: lodash 4.17.20 -> 4.17.21')
print('  tests: 412/412 pass | api-diff: no removals | bench: within 2%')
print('  verdict: SAFE TO MERGE')

title: Signature Upgrade rollback automation
description: Signature edition: Every sentinel-driven upgrade ships with a tested rollback: the previous lockfile, a database migration down-path, and a one-command revert. If production signals degrade after the upgrade, rollback is minutes, not a war room — the upgrade is only as safe as its undo.
method: Snapshot pre-upgrade state (lockfile, migrations, config); define the revert procedure; test revert in staging; trigger on signal degradation.
usage: Test the rollback before the upgrade, not after; keep the revert path working for the whole rollout window.

demo.code:
print('pre-upgrade snapshot: lockfile, migration v42 (down: v41)')
print('post-upgrade errors +3% -> TRIGGER ROLLBACK')
print('reverted to lockfile v41 in 4 minutes')

title: Signature Transitive dependency auditing
description: Signature edition: Your direct dependencies are the tip: sentinels audit the full transitive tree for vulnerabilities, license conflicts, and unmaintained packages. A clean direct dependency can pull in a vulnerable transitive one — the audit sees the whole tree, not just the top.
method: Resolve the full tree; scan every node for vulns/licenses/maintenance; report with the path that pulled each problem in.
usage: Audit on every lockfile change; fail on high-severity reachable vulns; track unmaintained packages for replacement.

title: Signature Stale dependency detection
description: Signature edition: Sentinels also watch for the opposite problem: dependencies pinned for years, accumulating unpatched vulnerabilities and making future upgrades painful. Staleness scoring (versions behind, months since release, open CVEs) prioritizes which ancient pins to modernize first.
method: Score each dep by versions-behind and age; flag unmaintained packages (no release in 2+ years); schedule modernization by risk.
usage: Review staleness quarterly; modernize the riskiest first; replace unmaintained packages deliberately.

title: Signature SBOM generation and tracking
description: Signature edition: A Software Bill of Materials lists every component in the shipped artifact — name, version, hash, license. Sentinels generate the SBOM at build time and track it across releases, so when the next Log4Shell hits, the question 'are we affected?' is a database query, not a fire drill.
method: Generate SBOM (CycloneDX/SPDX) at build; store per release; query across releases for affected components on new advisories.
usage: Generate for every release artifact; retain historically; make the affected-query a runbook step.

demo.code:
sbom = [{'name': 'log4j', 'version': '2.14.0'}]
print('SBOM components:', len(sbom))
print('advisory hits log4j -> query SBOM: AFFECTED (2.14.0 < 2.17.1)')

title: Signature Breaking-change detection via API diff
description: Signature edition: The sentinel diffs the public API surface between the old and new dependency versions — removed functions, changed signatures, altered defaults — and classifies the upgrade as patch/minor/major automatically. Semantic versioning claims are verified, not trusted.
method: Extract public API from both versions (AST/symbol tables); diff; classify (additive vs breaking); compare against the version bump claimed.
usage: Run API diff on every upgrade PR; treat a breaking change in a 'minor' bump as a red flag.

title: Signature Gradual rollout with canary
description: Signature edition: Even tested upgrades roll out gradually: canary a single service or 1% of traffic on the new dependency, watch error rates and latency, then widen. The sentinel automates the widening schedule and halts on regression — upgrades as controlled experiments.
method: Deploy new dep to canary slice; compare golden signals vs baseline; widen in steps (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%); auto-halt on regression.
usage: Define halt thresholds before rollout; keep the old version one click away during the whole rollout.

demo.code:
steps = [1, 10, 50, 100]
for s in steps:
    print(f'  rollout {s}%: errors nominal -> widen')
print('upgrade complete across fleet')

title: Signature Lockfile pinning and hashing
description: Signature edition: Sentinels enforce that every build uses exact pinned versions with content hashes (package-lock.json, Cargo.lock, poetry.lock). Pinning makes builds reproducible and upgrades deliberate: a version changes only when the sentinel proposes it, never because 'latest' moved overnight.
method: Commit lockfiles; verify hashes at install; CI fails on unpinned or hash-mismatched installs; upgrades modify the lockfile through the sentinel flow.
usage: Commit lockfiles for apps (not always for libraries); verify in CI; review lockfile diffs like code.

demo.code:
import hashlib
pin = {'lodash': '4.17.21'}
h = hashlib.sha256(pin['lodash'].encode()).hexdigest()[:10]
print(f'pinned lodash==4.17.21 (hash {h}) — reproducible install verified')
